$comment: Surface classification, per model. Every mesh in both assets carries exactly one material, so a material name identifies a surface. Nothing was renamed, regrouped or split in Blender to produce these tables - see README.md.
$paintable: Exactly one class is paintable. Body colour applies to every material in that class and to nothing else.
$wheels: The classes rim / rim_badge / tyre also identify which meshes are wheels, which is how CarModel splits wheels from body without relying on node names (all four wheels are named 'WheelFL' in the asset). Rim finish applies to 'rim' only — tyres stay black and the centre-cap badge keeps its logo.
$interior: interior_main is ONE material covering the whole cabin tub — seats, dashboard, steering wheel and door cards are a single mesh, so seat colour and dash colour cannot be separated without cutting geometry. Tinting it multiplies its baseColor texture. interior_trim (door tops, dash rail) is flat black with no texture and takes a colour directly.
$roof: soft_top identifies the roof canvas and its stitching decal. CarModel also uses it to find the whole roof part (canvas, decal, rear window, frame) so the roof-down state can hide all four together — hiding only the canvas would leave the rear window floating.
$normalisation: Look up a material by stripping a trailing '.NNN' duplicate suffix (M_Tire_Max.002 -> M_Tire_Max). Those suffixes are per-wheel copies of identical materials, not distinct surfaces. Note M_LightGlassNormal_OrangeLow. ends in a bare dot with no digits, so the rule leaves it alone.
$trap: M_CarPaint_Trim_PlasticSmoothBlack_Max contains 'CarPaint' but is the GLOSS BLACK trim on the front bumper, rear bumper and skirts. Matching materials by substring paints the grille surround body colour. Match exact names only.
$complete: complete:true means the table is expected to cover every material in the asset, so anything missing is drift and CarModel warns. complete:false means partial coverage is intended and unmapped surfaces are simply never touched.

mods.$comment: Mod assets are not part of either car, but they are recoloured by the same mechanism, so they classify the same way. This one table is shared by both generations and is merged over whichever model table is loaded. See mx5-mod-modelling-brief.md §3.
mods.$why: Naming a mod's paint material MOD_BodyPaint puts it in the body_paint class, so the existing paint picker recolours it with no new code at all. Same for MOD_Rim and the wheel-finish picker. That is the whole point of routing mods through this table rather than giving them their own colour plumbing.
mods.$caliper: MOD_CaliperPaint maps to a class no base asset uses. CarConfig.caliperColor already exists and is inert because neither car has a separate caliper mesh; the first wheel mod that ships one makes that control work.
mods.$newClasses: mod_accent, mod_carbon, mod_alloy, mod_rubber, mod_titanium and caliper do not appear in either car. They exist so a mod can declare a surface the app deliberately never tints.

nd.$model: Sketchfab "2016 Mazda MX-5 Miata" by Galaxy Car Showroom. Material names are self-describing, so this table was read straight off them.

roofLining.$comment: Loose parts of the cabin mesh that are really roof lining, and so must hide when the roof does. Hiding the roof part alone leaves an inner shell behind, because the artist modelled the lining as part of the interior tub. Identified by eye using the in-app "roof islands" debug view — bounding boxes cannot tell lining from cabin trim.
roofLining.$keys: Stable ids from islandKey(): triangleCount@localCentre. Deliberately not list indices, which shift whenever the candidate filter changes.
roofLining.$cutAboveY: Some parts are lining at the top and A-pillar trim lower down, so no whole-part rule separates them. When set, triangles above this world height (metres, ground = 0) are treated as lining too — but only within parts that already sit inside the roof volume. null disables it.

na.$model: Sketchfab "1990 Mazda Miata NA" by Ricy. Its materials are named Material_71, Material_230 ... which say nothing. This table was built by inspecting WHICH OBJECTS use each material, e.g. Material_71 is used by hood/leftdoor/rigthdoor/trunk/frontbumper/rearfender/f fender/rearbumper/Apillar/popuplight/americanjapaneserearpanel - unambiguously the paint. Only the surfaces the configurator drives are mapped; the other ~80 materials are deliberately left unclassified, so `complete` is false and no drift warning is raised. Material_70 (mirror housings + the alternate European rear panel) is body-coloured on a real NA, so it joins body_paint; Material_76 is the mirror glass.
